message.content:
This looks like a CBP ruling on the IndeeLift People Picker Upper. I recall it being classified in 8428.90, "Other lifting, handling, loading or unloading machinery," though I'm not certain. The alternatives I considered were 8427 (fork-lift trucks), 8425 (jacks and hoists), 8428.90.0290 and 9021 (orthopedic appliances).

Heading 8425 covers pulley tackle, hoists, winches, capstans, and jacks. This device is a powered lifting apparatus with an actuator and a mounting seat, so it doesn't fit as a jack or hoist. Heading 9021 covers appliances worn or carried to compensate for a defect or disability, and a stationary lift doesn't qualify. Patient lifts have been classified in 8428.90, and I believe this ruling did the same.

The 8428.90 subheadings run as follows: 8428.90.02 (Other machinery), 8428.90.0290 (Other), and 8428.90.03 (Other), with 8428.90.0390 under it. I'm not sure which applies, so I'll go with 8428.90.0290.

{"hts_code": "8428.90.0290", "reason": "A battery-powered, actuator-driven personal lifting device that raises a person from floor level is other lifting/handling machinery of heading 8428, not a hoist or jack of 8425 or an orthopedic appliance of 9021."}
